description: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate ({fb.rate}, packets of {fb.packet_bytes} bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries {la.rate}. Link lc joins r and c and carries only {lc.rate} with a one-way delay of {lc.delay}: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, {lc.queue.parts.fa} for fa and {lc.queue.parts.fb} for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of {lc.queue.length} packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is {fa.type}. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

lc.queue.parts.fa.meaning: the part of link lc for flow fa (fb's part is fixed at 0.5; the parts are divided by their sum)

lc.queue.length.meaning: most packets each of the two queues of the scheduler holds

fa.type.meaning: TCP congestion control of flow fa
